title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Forwarding the 'Reply Opinion of the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Question of Whether Judges Can Be Appointed and Removed Along with the Term of the People's Congress'
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Forwarding the "Reply Opinion of the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Whether Judges Can Be Appointed or Removed Concurrently with the Term of the People's Congress"

Fa [2003] No. 132

To all local people's courts at various levels nationwide, all maritime courts, and courts at various levels of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

We hereby forward to you the "Reply Opinion of the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Whether Judges Can Be Appointed or Removed Concurrently with the Term of the People's Congress" for your compliance.

July 29, 2003

Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress

Reply Opinion on Whether Judges Can Be Appointed or Removed Concurrently with the Term of the People's Congress

Fa Gong Wei Fu Zi [2003] No. 10

To the Supreme People's Court:

We have received the letter from the Political Department of the Supreme People's Court dated June 11, 2003 (Fa Zheng [2003] No. 85). After study, we hereby reply as follows:

According to the provisions of the Constitution and the Organic Law of the People's Courts, the term of office of the president of a people's court at any level is the same as the term of office of the corresponding people's congress. For vice presidents, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, judges, and members of the judicial committee, their term of office is not limited by the term of the people's congress. Therefore, there is no need for reappointment after the expiration of each term of the people's congress at any level.

July 14, 2003
